title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. X is a topos and u: Z -> Phi is a monomorphism of abelian sheaves. Write Psi = Coker u, so there is a short exact sequence 0 -> Z -> Phi -> Psi -> 0. (The page writes 'Coker Phi' and 'Coker i'; both mean Coker u.) Two hypotheses are imposed:
(a) Psi is Z-flat. Hence Phi is flat too, being an extension of flat sheaves.
(b) For every i>0, the sheaves Lambda^i_Z Phi and Gamma^i_Z Phi are flasque, and stay flasque after tensoring with any abelian sheaf.

Step b'). By induction and devissage, Gamma^i Phi (x) Lambda^j Phi is flasque whenever i+j>0. Flasque is in the SGA4 sense: acyclic on every object.

Step alpha). The sequence 0 -> Gamma^i Phi -> Gamma^i Phi (x) Phi -> Gamma^i Phi (x) Psi -> 0 is exact because Psi is flat. A quotient of a flasque sheaf by a flasque subsheaf is flasque, so Gamma^i Phi (x) Psi is flasque for i>0. The same devissage, using the filtration of Lambda^j Phi with graded pieces Lambda^j Psi and Lambda^{j-1} Psi, gives the general case Gamma^i Phi (x) Lambda^j Psi.

Step beta). Form the bigraded sheaf of algebras K_u = Gamma^*_Z Phi (x) Lambda^*_Z Psi.
- Its differential d is the unique PD-derivation that is zero on Lambda^* Psi and equals the projection Phi -> Psi on Phi. Concretely, d(x^[i]) = x^[i-1] (x) x-bar.
- This is the divided-power Koszul complex attached to the short exact sequence of flat sheaves, i.e. the PD de Rham complex of Gamma(Phi) relative to the 'coordinate' Psi.
- In each weight n it reads Gamma^n Phi -> Gamma^{n-1} Phi (x) Psi -> ... -> Lambda^n Psi.
- It is a resolution of Gamma^n(Z) = Z.T^[n]. So K_u resolves the divided-power polynomial algebra Z{T} = Gamma_Z(Z), with T sent to 1 in Ker(Phi -> Psi).

Step gamma). Divided and exterior powers commute with base change and flatness is preserved. So for any sheaf of commutative rings k, K_u (x) k = Gamma_k Phi_k (x) Lambda_k Psi_k resolves k{T}, and its terms with i>0 are flasque.

Purpose (next page). Take global sections K(X,u,k). In weight n, every term of the resolution is flasque except the last, Lambda^n Psi. A dimension-shifting argument therefore shows that H^{n,j} of the global sections maps isomorphically to H^j(X,k).T^[n] for j <= n, and vanishes for j > n; this is the triangle drawn at the bottom of the next page. A relative version holds for f_*.

Outcome. One gets a functorial, strictly (graded-)commutative bigraded dg algebra with divided powers whose cohomology is H^*(X,k) (x) Gamma(T) in the range j <= n. Products respect the weight. This is a 'resolving sheaf' approach to divided-power (de Rham / crystalline-type) structures on cohomology, presented under the heading 'Faisceaux resolvants du topos De Rham'.
errors: Notational slips: 'Coker Phi' in (a) and 'Coker i' in the definition of Psi should both read Coker u.
The isomorphism at the boundary j = n (where Lambda^n Psi is not assumed flasque) is not argued on this page; it does hold, by dimension shifting, since H^1 of the last flasque term vanishes.
Hypothesis (b) on Lambda^i Phi is more than is needed for alpha) beyond the devissage; this is harmless.
No construction of a sheaf Phi satisfying (a) and (b) is given here. The existence of such 'resolving sheaves' on a general topos is the real issue and is left open on this page.

ideas.what: Divided-power Koszul complex Gamma^{n-j}Phi (x) Lambda^j Psi resolving Gamma^n of the kernel of a surjection of flat modules/sheaves
ideas.modern_name: PD Koszul complex / PD Poincare lemma
ideas.where_published: Illusie, Complexe cotangent et deformations I, ch. I 4.3

ideas.what: Flasqueness of tensor products of divided and exterior powers by devissage
Global sections of K_u give a functorial bigraded PD-cdga computing H^*(X,k) (x) Gamma(T) in the triangle j <= weight, zero above it
ideas.modern_name: strictly commutative divided-power cochain model in a weight range; weight-graded resolution of O(G_a^sharp)
ideas.usually_credited_to: unsure; related ideas in Cartan's PD simplicial forms and Karoubi's commutative cochains

missed.claim: Grothendieck sketches 'resolving sheaves' Z -> Phi on an arbitrary topos whose divided and exterior powers are flasque. With them he builds a functorial, strictly commutative PD bigraded algebra computing cohomology tensored with Gamma(T) in a triangular range. The weight grading via T^[n] (with T^[n]T^[m] = binom(n+m,n) T^[n+m]) sidesteps the usual Steenrod obstruction to commutative cochains: for example, cup squares in weight 2n pick up the even factor binom(2n,n).
missed.quote: on trouve que K_u est une résolution de Z{T} ... les Gamma^i_k Phi_k (x) Lambda^j_k Psi_k sont flasques pour i>0
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a sheaf-theoretic, weight-graded route to integral commutative/PD cochain models. Gamma(T) is the ring of functions on G_a^sharp, which links it to recent de Rham-stack, G_a^sharp and binomial-ring approaches to integral homotopy theory (Toen's schematization, Bhatt-Lurie, derived binomial rings). Whether this explicit triangle-range construction appears in that literature is unclear.

deep.surprise_reason: The algebra itself, the PD Koszul resolution, is standard. The use made of it is less standard: functorial resolving sheaves on a topos giving a strictly commutative PD model of H^*(X,k) (x) Gamma(T) in a triangular range, framed as the 'topos De Rham'. It is an unpublished, mildly original construction, but its novelty against Cartan, Karoubi and later work is uncertain.
transcription_corrections: Heading reads 'Faisceaux résolvants du topos De Rham'.
In alpha) the exponent is a 1 (Lambda^1_Z Psi), as transcribed; the general j case follows by devissage.
'Coker Phi' and 'Coker i' are as written by Grothendieck; both mean Coker u.
